Provenance.drafts: Two base rounds plus a targeted inpaint, all via ComfyUI MCP against the U3 Building clause (anchor-palette blockout -> img2img, IPAdapterAdvanced vit-h style-transfer w0.9 against market.png as the style reference). Round A (seed 700200, denoise 0.8, 4 candidates): #1 read as a pretty barn with zero smithy identity, #3 grew a chapel-cross roof finial off-brand, #4's fireplace face read wrong; #2 (open bays, anvil pad, forge-fire glow) was the strongest composition but had no true anvil silhouette yet -- kept as the base for inpainting rather than rerolled. Round B (seed 700300, denoise 0.8, 4 candidates, alternate framing): all four missed structurally (cottage plus wood shed, two separate buildings, plain cottage, confused stall plus oven) -- abandoned; round A's #2 stayed the base.
Provenance.paintoverNote: Targeted inpaint (seed 700800, denoise 0.5, mask over the anvil/fire-bay pad only) against round A's #2, 4 candidates: #1/#3/#4 turned the anvil into a pot, a black lump and a box stove respectively; #2 produced a true black anvil on its stump plus the glowing fire-bay behind it and was the winner. Shipped pixels are round A's composition with only the anvil pad re-painted -- confirmed identical to the picked candidate by a pixel-exact diff against the full-size PICK render.
Provenance.aiDisclosure: AI-generated (SDXL base 1.0 + pixel-art-xl LoRA) diffuse, two ComfyUI KSampler passes (base seed 700200 @ denoise 0.8, then a masked inpaint seed 700800 @ denoise 0.5 over the anvil/fire-bay only), IPAdapterAdvanced (vit-h, style transfer, weight 0.9) referencing market.png so palette and lighting lock to the shipped Shop -- read directly from both PNGs' own embedded ComfyUI workflow JSON, not quoted from memory. DEVIATION from cutout.py: background removed via a deterministic flood-fill alpha matte (border-color median, border-seeded flood-fill of the core-background mask, then a fixed ~5px feather ring) rather than the BiRefNet model cutout.py wraps -- this render's backdrop measured near-uniform (border std < 1.2 per channel on every edge) so a segmentation-model pass bought nothing; cutout.py/BiRefNet remains the tool of record for gradient or busy backgrounds. Cropped to the alpha content box, then BOX-downsampled straight to 72x81 (no hard quantization) -- the same recipe market.png's own committed pixels were produced by. This is forge's first build.json; the asset previously had no provenance record at all.
